# Customized Fragments

## `highlight` and `highlight-current`


Despite the default
<span class="fragment highlight-green" data-fragment-index="1">green</span>,
<span class="fragment highlight-red" data-fragment-index="2">red</span>, and
<span class="fragment highlight-blue" data-fragment-index="3">blue</span>,
there are three colors available for this template:

- <span class="fragment highlight-forestgreen" data-fragment-index="1">forest green</span>,
- <span class="fragment highlight-indianred" data-fragment-index="2">indian red</span>, and
- <span class="fragment highlight-steelblue" data-fragment-index="3">steel blue</span>.

Code:

```html
- <span class="fragment highlight-forestgreen" data-fragment-index="1">forest green</span>,
- <span class="fragment highlight-indianred" data-fragment-index="2">indian red</span>, and
- <span class="fragment highlight-steelblue" data-fragment-index="3">steel blue</span>.

```


Noted that, class `fragment-` with `highlight-forestgreen`, `highlight-indianred`, `highlight-steelblue` also highlight the fragment of current index with font-weight `bold`.

## `highlight-current`

Similar to the use of `highlight`, but the effects will disappear if next fragment index is triggered.

Code:

```html
- <span class="fragment highlight-current-forestgreen" data-fragment-index="1">forest green</span>,
- <span class="fragment highlight-current-indianred" data-fragment-index="2">indian red</span>, and
- <span class="fragment highlight-current-steelblue" data-fragment-index="3">steel blue</span>.
```

Output:

- <span class="fragment highlight-current-forestgreen" data-fragment-index="1">forest green</span>,
- <span class="fragment highlight-current-indianred" data-fragment-index="2">indian red</span>, and
- <span class="fragment highlight-current-steelblue" data-fragment-index="3">steel blue</span>.


## `highlight-bold` and `highlight-current-bold`

When using `highlight-bold` and `highlight-current-bold` the original color is inherited. Both of them highlights the text with bold and slight shading.

Code:

```html
- <span class="fragment highlight-current-bold" data-fragment-index="1">bold (current)</span>,
- <span class="fragment highlight-bold" data-fragment-index="2">bold (persistent)</span>, and
- <span class="fragment highlight-current-bold" data-fragment-index="3">bold (current)</span>
```

- <span class="fragment highlight-current-bold" data-fragment-index="1">bold (current)</span>,
- <span class="fragment highlight-bold" data-fragment-index="2">bold (persistent)</span>, and
- <span class="fragment highlight-current-bold" data-fragment-index="3">bold (current)</span>

## `blur`

Blur the text in the beginning, and then unveil it.

Code:

```html
- <span class="fragment blur" data-fragment-index="1">Blurred text.</span>
```

- <span class="fragment blur" data-fragment-index="1">Blurred text.</span>

# Inline tags and images

## {}

### `rtag`, `ltag` and `nftag`

Code:

```
- Hello World [a no-floating tag]{.nftag fragment-index=1 .fragment}
- Hello World [a align-right tag]{.rtag fragment-index=2 .fragment}
- Hello World [a align-left tag]{.ltag fragment-index=3 .fragment}
```

- Hello World [a no-floating tag]{.nftag fragment-index=1 .fragment}
- Hello World [a align-right tag]{.rtag fragment-index=2 .fragment}
- Hello World [a align-left tag]{.ltag fragment-index=3 .fragment}

### Inline image

Code:

```
- Hello, this (![](non-existing.png){.inlineimg}) is an inline image.
```

- Hello, this (![](non-existing.png){.inlineimg}) is an inline image.

## Dealing with overflow {.scrollable}

This is a scrollable page, with a scrollable container.
Typically it is not a good idea to show a scrollable container in a scrollable page; this makes presenter struggle to scroll the correct target.

### Scrollable container
::: {.scroll-container style="overflow-y: scroll; height: 800px;"}
This is a scrollable container.
![](background.png){width="1920px" fig-align="center"}
:::

## Dealing with overflow {.unlisted}

Decision logic:

- When Contents overflow:
  1. Create a new slide with the same title with `{.unlisted}` (to not show repeat entries in TOC).
  2. If 1. is not applicable (e.g., image itself overflow):
     - Use `{.scrollable}` on a single page. This way the **Slide Heading** (`## <Slide Heading>`) is not persistent on scroll.
     - When one needs the slide heading or some content on the top persist on scrolling, use [Scrollable container](#scrollable-container).


## Highlight in background at arbitrary position {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="box1" .custom-box style="--left: 200px; --top: 100px; --width: 250px; --height: 70px; --bg-color: #2780e3; --radius: 20px;"}
:::

- Create a `.custom-box` to highlight contents from the background at arbitrary position.


## Highlight in background at arbitrary position {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="box1" .custom-box style="--left: 280px; --top: 230px; --width: 360px; --height: 70px; --bg-color: #2780e3; --radius: 20px;"}
:::


- Create a `.custom-box` to highlight contents from the background at arbitrary position.
- While this is visually appealing, don't overuse it because it makes the slide hard to maintain.
